# Behavioral Specification: TL-UL SRAM Adapter

## 1. Purpose

The TL-UL SRAM adapter bridges TileLink-UL (TL-UL) bus transactions to a simple SRAM-like memory interface. It accepts single-beat read and write requests from the bus, converts them into memory requests, and returns the appropriate TL-UL responses. It also enforces the project’s TL-UL protocol rules and supports optional bus integrity features.

The adapter is intended to make an SRAM-like memory appear as a well-behaved TL-UL device.

---

## 2. Configuration

The adapter is configurable at instantiation. Its configuration affects observable behavior as follows:

| Configuration option | Behavioral effect |
|---|---|
| SRAM address width | Determines the width of the memory address presented during each request. |
| SRAM data width | Determines the memory interface data width. It must be a multiple of the TL-UL data width. |
| Outstanding transaction count | Limits how many TL-UL requests may be in flight at one time. The default is one. |
| Byte-write access | When enabled, sub-word write requests are accepted. When disabled, any write that is not a full-width write is rejected with an error response. |
| Write rejection | When enabled, all write requests are rejected with error responses. |
| Read rejection | When enabled, all read requests are rejected with error responses. |
| Command integrity checking | When enabled, the command integrity field of every incoming request is validated. |
| Response integrity generation | When enabled, the adapter generates the response integrity field for every response. |
| Data integrity generation | When enabled, the adapter generates data integrity bits for read response data. |
| Data integrity pass-through | When enabled, data integrity bits are passed through from the bus to memory on writes and from memory back to the bus on reads. |
| Error data values | Defines the data pattern returned when the response does not carry valid read data. Separate values are used for instruction-fetch and non-instruction-fetch requests. |

Valid configurations must not enable both data integrity generation and data integrity pass-through. Valid configurations must not reject both reads and writes.

---

## 3. TL-UL Request Handling

### 3.1 Request Acceptance

The adapter shall accept a TL-UL request only when it has sufficient tracking resources for another outstanding transaction. If the configured number of outstanding transactions is already in use, the adapter shall hold the request until resources become available.

The adapter shall process requests in order and shall return responses in the same order as the corresponding requests were accepted.

For each response, the returned source identifier and size shall match those of the original request. The response opcode shall indicate a data response for a read and a write acknowledgement for a write.

### 3.2 Protocol Validation

The adapter shall validate every incoming request before forwarding it to memory. A request that violates any of the following rules shall not be forwarded to memory and shall instead be answered with an error response:

- The opcode must be a defined TL-UL opcode.
- Reserved request fields must be zero.
- The address must be aligned to the requested size.
- The size and byte mask must be consistent.
- The byte mask must be contiguous when required by the TL-UL protocol.
- The access must be permitted by the configured read/write rejection policy.
- If byte-write access is disabled, a write must be a full-width write.
- An instruction-fetch request is permitted only when the instruction-fetch enable control is in a valid enabled state.
- If command integrity checking is enabled, the command integrity field must validate correctly.

If any of these checks fail, the adapter shall return a TL-UL error response. The response data field shall use the configured error data pattern selected by the instruction-fetch attribute of the request.

---

## 4. Memory Request Behavior

### 4.1 Request Presentation

For a request that passes validation, the adapter shall present a memory request with the following properties:

- The request is presented only while the request is being processed.
- The request is considered accepted by memory only when the memory-side request and grant indications are both asserted.
- The adapter shall not present a new memory request until the previous request has been accepted or discarded.
- The write-enable indication is asserted for writes and deasserted for reads.
- The memory address is derived from the TL-UL address and is aligned to the SRAM word.
- The memory request type indicates whether the original request is an instruction fetch.

If a request is erroneous, the adapter shall not present any memory request for that transaction.

### 4.2 SRAM Words Wider Than the TL-UL Data Width

When the SRAM data width is larger than the TL-UL data width, the SRAM word is treated as multiple TL-UL words. The low address bits that select the TL-UL word within the SRAM word are used to place the TL-UL transaction on the correct portion of the memory interface.

- For writes, the write data and write mask are placed in the selected TL-UL word position.
- For reads, the requested TL-UL word position is selected from the memory read data.

---

## 5. Write Transactions

### 5.1 Normal Writes

For an accepted write request, the adapter shall:

- Assert the memory write-enable indication.
- Present the write data on the memory write data bus.
- Present a write mask that enables only the byte lanes selected by the original TL-UL request.
- Drive unselected write data byte lanes to zero.
- Return a write acknowledgement response after the write has been accepted by the memory interface.

When byte-write access is disabled, only full-width writes are accepted. Any partial write is rejected with an error response.

### 5.2 Writes with Stored Data Integrity

When data integrity is stored in memory, the integrity bits associated with the written SRAM word are written together with the data.

If the write is a partial write and the adapter is configured to support byte writes with integrity protection, the adapter shall ensure the entire SRAM word and its integrity field remain consistent. To do this, it may internally read the target word first, merge the requested bytes into it, recompute or update the integrity field, and then write the full word back. The host-visible write acknowledgement shall complete only after the resulting write has been accepted.

---

## 6. Read Transactions

### 6.1 Normal Reads

For an accepted read request, the adapter shall:

- Assert the memory read request.
- Wait for the memory read data to be returned.
- Return a TL-UL data response containing the requested bytes.

If data integrity is not passed through, the read response data shall be masked so that only byte lanes requested by the original request are delivered. Unrequested byte lanes shall be returned as zero.

If data integrity is passed through, the adapter shall return the selected SRAM word data together with its integrity field. Unrequested byte lanes may contain memory contents but are not considered meaningful.

### 6.2 Read Errors from Memory

The memory interface provides a two-bit error status with a correctable-error indication and an uncorrectable-error indication.

- A correctable-error indication shall not cause the TL-UL response to be marked as an error.
- An uncorrectable-error indication shall cause the read response to be marked as an error.
- When an uncorrectable read error is reported, the read response data shall use the configured error data pattern rather than the memory data.

---

## 7. Response Behavior

### 7.1 Response Types

- A write transaction shall receive a write acknowledgement response.
- A read transaction shall receive a data response.
- A rejected transaction shall receive the same response type as if it were a valid transaction of its request class, but with the error indication asserted.

### 7.2 Response Data on Non-Read Responses

Whenever a response does not carry valid read data, including write acknowledgements and error responses, the response data bus shall still be driven to a defined value. This value shall be selected from the configured error data patterns based on whether the original request was an instruction fetch.

### 7.3 Response Backpressure

The adapter shall hold a response valid until the response is accepted by the TL-UL host. Once accepted, the adapter shall retire the corresponding transaction tracking entry.

---

## 8. Integrity Behavior

### 8.1 Command Integrity Checking

When command integrity checking is enabled, every incoming request shall be checked. If the command integrity check fails:

- The request shall not be forwarded to memory.
- An error response shall be returned for that request.
- A sticky integrity-error output shall be asserted and shall remain asserted until reset.

The sticky integrity-error output is a module-level indication independent of the per-transaction error response.

### 8.2 Response Integrity Generation

When response integrity generation is enabled, every TL-UL response shall carry a valid response integrity field. When disabled, no response integrity is generated.

### 8.3 Data Integrity Modes

The adapter supports three data integrity behaviors:

- **No data integrity:** The memory data path contains only data bits. No data integrity field is generated or passed through.
- **Data integrity pass-through:** The memory data path contains both data and integrity bits. Write integrity bits from the request are forwarded to memory with the write data. Read integrity bits from memory are forwarded to the TL-UL response with the read data.
- **Data integrity generation:** The adapter computes the data integrity bits for read response data. The memory data path contains only data bits.

Data integrity generation and data integrity pass-through shall not be enabled at the same time.

When a response carries no valid read data, the data integrity field, if present, shall be driven to a defined benign value rather than to a value derived from memory.

---

## 9. Instruction Fetch Handling

The adapter shall distinguish instruction-fetch requests from other requests.

- An instruction-fetch request is allowed only when the instruction-fetch enable control is in a valid enabled state.
- If the enable control is not in that state, the request shall be rejected with an error response.
- For accepted requests, the adapter shall indicate the instruction-fetch property on the memory request.
- The error data pattern returned for rejected or erroneous instruction-fetch transactions may differ from the pattern used for non-instruction-fetch transactions.

---

## 10. Reset and Output State

On reset:

- All in-flight transaction tracking shall be cleared.
- No TL-UL response shall be asserted.
- No memory request shall be asserted.
- The write-enable indication shall be deasserted.
- The sticky integrity-error output shall be cleared.

At all times outside reset, the adapter shall drive its outputs to defined known values. It shall not leave response, request, address, write-data, or write-mask outputs undriven.

---

## 11. Configuration Restrictions

The following configurations are invalid:

- Both read rejection and write rejection enabled, since the adapter would be unable to process any transaction.
- Both data integrity generation and data integrity pass-through enabled.
- An SRAM data width that is not a multiple of the TL-UL data width.
- An SRAM data width that is not byte-granular.

The adapter shall be configured with at least one outstanding transaction.
